Done. The saved edit is verified by two independent real forward passes. Final summary:

## What I changed

**`heads.head.weight` (rows 58 and 65 only) and `heads.head.bias` (entries 58 and 65)** — a rank-1, symmetric, additive edit; all other head rows and the entire backbone are untouched.

1. **Diagnosis.** The head's 58-vs-65 direction `W[58]−W[65]` is badly aligned (cos ≈ 0.46) with the actual class-mean difference in the final-LN feature space, and the raw mean-difference direction `d` is contaminated: gull look-alike classes (59, 60, 61, 63, 64, 83…) lie at ±(1–14) along it, so boosting along raw `d` steals their images. The 13 practice pair errors split into 58→65 (6), 58→63 (5), 65→58 (4, one image 58→61), and no 1-D rule on `d` could fix both error groups (they overlap in `d`-projection).

2. **Direction construction (statistics only, no training).** Using the within-class scatter of the gull family (classes 44, 57, 59–64, 83 plus 58/65 residuals), I whitened `d` with a *partial* exponent: `v ∝ U (Uᵀd) / ev^0.2`, normalized. This interpolates between the raw mean-difference (p=0, unsafe, LOO 10/30 errors) and full Fisher whitening (p=1, catastrophically overfits, LOO 12/30, broke ~70 other images in simulation). At p≈0.2–0.5 the projected scores of all error groups land strictly on the correct side of the midpoint — **leave-one-out over all 30 pair images gave 0/30 errors**, and other-class images sit within ±1.1 of the midpoint (vs ±20 for raw `d`).

3. **The edit.** With `t` the midpoint of the two class-mean projections of `v`: `W[58] += 4.2·v`, `b[58] −= 4.2·t`, `W[65] −= 4.2·v`, `b[65] += 4.2·t`. This shifts row 58 up and row 65 down strictly along the new discriminative axis, leaving every other class's logits unchanged in the directions that matter. Gains were chosen from an exact simulation grid (replaying cached `head_in` features through candidate weights — exact, since the head is linear) requiring: pair errors fixed, zero pair regressions, minimal other-class breaks, and a safety margin; shielding other rows was tested and rejected (it caused 9 breaks).

## What I measured (practice images, 2875 imgs, ~14/class)

- **Pair accuracy (58 vs 65): 43.3% → 96.7%** (13 errors → 1; fixed 6×58→65, 5×58→63, 4×65→58, 1×65→61; zero pair regressions).
- **Overall accuracy: 84.14% → 84.59%** (up, not just within the −0.3 tolerance). Net effect on other classes: 3 near-tie images flip wrong (White_necked_Raven, Nashville_Warbler, Marsh_Wren — each within ~1 logit of the decision boundary before the edit).
- Verified through the real edited forward pass (not just replay): feature stream is bit-identical to the original (edit touches only the head rows), and both metrics reproduce exactly.
- Robustness checks: pair margins improved from 17 images < 0.5 logit to 5; results are stable for gains 3.8–4.4 and midpoint shifts ±0.04; the LOO result (0/30) indicates the underlying 1-D rule, not just these 30 images, carries the signal.

The remaining risk is the thin-margin tail (3 broken other-class images on practice; ~36 others within 0.25 logit of a flip at this gain), which is balanced against fixing 16 of 17 pair errors — on the held-out set the large pair gain (+53 pts on practice) should dominate the ≤0.3-pt overall allowance.
